Earnings Whispers has EPS at $0.88. Short interest: unavailable.
view: The quarter itself is close to settled. Elastic has beaten its own guide on each of the last five prints. Last quarter it beat revenue by about $8.5M and sales-led by about $6.5M (Q1 guide $392-393M, actual $399M). cRPO is growing 20% cc against 15-17% revenue growth, about 70% of FY27 sales-led is said to be in committed backlog, and the comparable from a year ago is soft (Q2 FY26 cRPO +15% cc, $971M). So a typical beat to about $414M sales-led (+18.6% y/y, against 18% last quarter) and holding cRPO near 20% are the likely outcomes. Citi's check of a federal partner (September bookings up more than 60%) and strong security peers this month (PANW, CRWD, S, OKTA, ZS all up) help. That typical beat is, however, exactly the buy-side bogey, so it is in the price. The reaction will turn on the H2 guide. Elastic's habit is to pass the beat through and add about $1M to the year: last quarter FY sales-led went $1,680.5M to $1,688M at the midpoint, on a $6.5M beat. Repeated, that gives roughly $1.695-1.70B, at the bogey rather than above it, and a Q3 guide at its usual ~17-18% growth lands near $437-440M, below the $443M bogey. That is the same setup as November 2025, when a beat-and-raise with an H2 guide in line with consensus fell 15%. Against that, the price has given back the whole August reaction in four weeks on sector and peer news, not company news. This month's tape has paid accelerating infrastructure prints (NET +17% gap, FROG +27%, DOCN +11%) and crushed decelerating ones (DDOG, DT, TEAM, TWLO). Elastic's cRPO above revenue is the acceleration case, and management has already said growth builds to a Q4 peak. So the bar is lower than it was, but whether the guide clears the bogey is close to even. I lean slightly up because the stock already holds a de-rating that its own evidence does not show. That lean is not large enough to trade.
unpriced: Possibly the gap between ESTC's own evidence and its price: a 27% fall from the 2026-10-26 peak tied to software-sector and observability-peer prints, while cRPO, federal and security inputs point to an intact quarter. The deciding line, the H2 sales-led guide against a ~$443M / >$1.70B bogey, is near a coin flip on Elastic's guiding habit, so I cannot show the price is wrong on it.

recommendation.reason: A Q2 beat is very likely (5 of 5 prior beats; cRPO 20% cc running ahead of revenue; an easy comp), but the published buy-side bogey already assumes the typical beat. The reaction turns on the H2 guide, and Elastic's practice of passing the beat through puts it near the bogey, not clearly above it; that setup cost 15% in November 2025. The 27% sector-driven de-rating lowers the bar enough to lean up, not enough to reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: cRPO growth below about 18% cc, or a Q3 sales-led guide under about $437M with FY sales-led raised by less than the beat, would make the print a repeat of November 2025 and send it sharply down. A FY sales-led raise above $1.70B with cRPO at 21% or more would flip it firmly up.

self_critique: The strongest case against a slight lean up: Elastic's guide habit, together with a bogey already above that habit, is the exact November 2025 pattern, and in this tape software names whose guides only match expectations have been punished hard (DT, DDOG, TEAM, TWLO). Today's idiosyncratic -6.8% on a large block could also be informed de-risking I cannot see. The strongest case for more upside: the stock now holds none of the August reacceleration, while cRPO at 20% and backlog cover make the reacceleration close to mechanical, so even an in-line H2 guide could bring relief. The two roughly cancel. I leave the number at 56 and make no call.
approach_notes: P6 (taking the run-in apart against peers and the sector) and P3's 'rebuild the line from parts' (the guide-habit arithmetic against the published bogey) did the most work here.
